paragraphs.text: 3.1 Introduction

runs.text: 3.1 Introduction

paragraphs.text: This chapter presents the software requirements and system design of the VR text-entry application. It covers the overall architecture, six input methods, swipe-recognition workflow, data logging and experimental design. Chapter 4 presents the implementation.

runs.text: This chapter presents the software requirements and system design of the VR text-entry application. It covers the overall architecture, six input methods, swipe-recognition workflow, data logging and experimental design. Chapter 4 presents the implementation.

paragraphs.text: 3.2 Software Requirements

runs.text: 3.2 Software Requirements

paragraphs.text: The application supports the implementation and evaluation of six input methods under consistent conditions. The requirements define system functions, interaction quality and data collection.

runs.text: The application supports the implementation and evaluation of six input methods under consistent conditions. The requirements define system functions, interaction quality and data collection.

paragraphs.text: 3.2.1 Functional Requirements

runs.text: 3.2.1 Functional Requirements

paragraphs.text: The system must provide a virtual QWERTY keyboard and support six methods: controller ray selection with trigger confirmation, controller ray selection with dwell confirmation, direct controller tapping, controller-based swipe typing, two-index-finger hand-tracked typing and ten-finger hand-tracked typing. It must display the target phrase and current transcription and support character entry, spaces, deletion and submission.

runs.text: The system must provide a virtual QWERTY keyboard and support six methods: controller ray selection with trigger confirmation, controller ray selection with dwell confirmation, direct controller tapping, controller-based swipe typing, two-index-finger hand-tracked typing and ten-finger hand-tracked typing. It must display the target phrase and current transcription and support character entry, spaces, deletion and submission.

paragraphs.text: Each method must provide appropriate feedback. Ray methods must show the targeted key and ray endpoint. Dwell selection must show activation progress. Controller tapping and hand-tracked typing must show contact feedback and prevent repeated activation from a single contact. Swipe typing must record the controller trajectory, rank word candidates and support candidate selection and correction. The system must also provide practice and formal testing stages and allow the researcher to select the participant code and active condition before each session.

runs.text: 3.2.2 Non-Functional Requirements

paragraphs.text: The application must remain stable and responsive, with minimal perceptible delay between input and visual feedback. The keyboard layout, dimensions, position, target-phrase display and visual design must remain consistent across conditions. This control limits interface-related variation.

paragraphs.text: 3.2.3 Data Collection Requirements

runs.text: 3.2.3 Data Collection Requirements

Each phrase-level record contains the participant code, input method, target phrase, transcribed phrase, start time, end time and duration. Event logs record key activations, deletions, corrections, total input actions and movement data where applicable.

paragraphs.text: 3.3 System Design

runs.text: 3.3 System Design

paragraphs.text: The system uses a modular architecture. All methods share the virtual keyboard, text manager, experiment manager and data logger. Method-specific components handle input and feedback. This structure supports consistent evaluation and separate implementation.

paragraphs.text: 3.3.1 Overall System Architecture

runs.text: 3.3.1 Overall System Architecture

paragraphs.text: The system contains five components: the VR input layer, text-entry method controller, virtual keyboard and text manager, experiment manager and data logger. The VR input layer receives controller or hand-tracking data. The active method interprets the input and sends a character or recognised word to the shared text manager.

paragraphs.text: The experiment manager controls the participant code, active condition, phrase sequence, practice stage and formal testing stage. The data logger stores interaction events and performance records.

runs.text: 3.3.3 Text-Entry Method Design

runs.text: 3.3.3.1 Trigger-Based Ray Selection

runs.text: 3.3.3.4 Controller-Based Swipe Typing

paragraphs.text: 3.3.4 Swipe Recognition Design

runs.text: 3.3.4 Swipe Recognition Design

paragraphs.text: The recogniser converts a continuous controller trajectory into ranked word candidates through three stages: trajectory capture and processing, candidate generation and ranking, and user correction.

runs.text: The recogniser converts a continuous controller trajectory into ranked word candidates through three stages: trajectory capture and processing, candidate generation and ranking, and user correction.

paragraphs.text: 3.3.4.1 Trajectory Capture and Processing

runs.text: 3.3.4.1 Trajectory Capture and Processing

paragraphs.text: Controller positions are sampled while the trigger is held and transformed from world coordinates to keyboard-relative coordinates.

runs.text: Controller positions are sampled while the trigger is held and transformed from world coordinates to keyboard-relative coordinates.

paragraphs.text: Processing removes near-duplicate points, smooths the path and resamples it to a fixed-length representation. The processed trajectory can then be compared with candidate word paths.

runs.text: Processing removes near-duplicate points, smooths the path and resamples it to a fixed-length representation. The processed trajectory can then be compared with candidate word paths.

paragraphs.text: 3.3.4.2 Candidate Generation and Ranking

runs.text: 3.3.4.2 Candidate Generation and Ranking

paragraphs.text: Candidates are drawn from an English vocabulary. Approximate starting and ending key positions restrict the search space.

runs.text: Candidates are drawn from an English vocabulary. Approximate starting and ending key positions restrict the search space.

paragraphs.text: The ranking score combines trajectory similarity, proximity to expected key positions and word frequency. The highest-ranked candidate is the Top-1 prediction, and the five highest-ranked candidates form the Top-5 list.

runs.text: The ranking score combines trajectory similarity, proximity to expected key positions and word frequency. The highest-ranked candidate is the Top-1 prediction, and the five highest-ranked candidates form the Top-5 list.
